summary: Art review of fx (post, particles, KO/WRECKED/SHOWTIME looks) at 1920x1080 in game on coast, city and mountain (chase cam: slow, cruise, top speed, slipstream, drift L1-L3, boost, hop/landing, light and heavy hits, player hurt), real-combat KO, WRECKED and SHOWTIME strips every 50-100 ms with and without the HUD, and sandbox particle close-ups. 0 __br.errors in every run. Strong points: the KO cut-in frame reads like a manga panel (black wedge KO lines, low 3/4 angle, inked orange POW star). The P5 red ray backdrop with halftone and slanted letterbox has real flavour. Heavy-hit POW stars are crisp, inked and comic. The drift tiers are colour-coded correctly. Speed sensation grows from cruise to top speed to boost. The damage edge pulse is clear. MSAA makes the post image cleaner than the raw render. Against a polished commercial stylised game it falls short where it matters most. (1) The KO hold's comic tone map uses absolute luminance: on coast the victim is red-brown on red rays, at night in the city every rider becomes one merged black silhouette, and on the mountain the victim is red on red, so the money shot has no clear subject on two of three tracks. (2) WRECKED is a half-strength comic look under a global red multiply, a muddy pink frame with the pelican half-hidden behind a blurred rider. (3) The grade multiplies the track tint over everything: whites go cream or orange, the coast sky turns teal, and the mountain's purple sunset collapses to orange-red, hurting hero readability everywhere. (4) The SHOWTIME hold shows no victim, just the burst and a carpet of identical puffs. Minor: one plain annulus sprite stands in for boost, block, sparkle, heal and other rings (the boost hoop round the torso looks like a debug gizmo); the landing dust is a perfect wreath of identical puffs; wind lines spawn ahead of the rider and slice through rivals; edge blur at plain top speed smears toon outlines; drift sparks are thin; the light-hit glow is a soft smudge. Evidence: shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/ (scripts *.mjs, frames k-*/r-*/h-*/c-*, sheets s-*.png, crops z-*.png, notes.txt).

issues.title: KO hold: the victim is not a clear subject. The comic look uses absolute-luminance thresholds, so the city turns every rider into one merged black silhouette and the mountain renders the victim red-on-red (src/fx/post/composite-glsl.ts fxKoLook + fxBurst)
issues.detail: Real heavy-swing KO, fx only (?stub=ui), 50 ms strips. Coast (shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/s-ko-key.png, k-ko-coast-noui-039/072.png): mid-tones map to FX_RED_DEEP and the backdrop rays are FX_RED/deep red, so the brown sloth victim is a red-brown body on red rays. Only its outline and white eye patches separate it. The unrelated capybara in the left foreground is the largest silhouette in frame, and the white pelican (attacker) pops more than the victim. City (shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/k-ko-city-039/072.png, s-ko-cm.png): night luma gives g < 0.3 everywhere, so victim, pelican, bikes and bystander are all flat FX_INK and overlap into one black mass. You cannot tell who is KO'd; only the popped helmet reads. Mountain (shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/k-ko-mtn-039/072.png): the sunset grade pushes everything into the red band, so the victim is a slightly lighter red on red rays, the weakest separation of the three. The brief's bar ('clear subject, strong composition') is missed on all three tracks, and badly on two.
issues.fix: 1) Re-centre the tone map on the subject. Add a uniform uKoMid = mean luma of a small box around cine.focus (CPU: one readPixels of a low bloom mip, or a 1x1 downsample, cached at the cut), and use g = (lk - uKoMid) * 1.5 + 0.52, so every track spans ink / red / paper. 2) Keep the reds for the backdrop: where the bg mask is 0 (subject), map mid-tones to paper with ink halftone instead of FX_RED_DEEP. 3) Cut the subject out like a sticker: a 3-4 px paper (or ink on a dark backdrop) rim where the depth mask crosses uSubjectDepth + uBgMargin (sample depth at +/- 2 px). 4) Push bystanders back: riders other than the victim render as a 50 % ink silhouette (pass their ids via a stencil or layer), or choose an azimuth where none sits between the camera and the victim. Verify that coast/city/mountain hold frames show the victim's face and limbs distinct from the rays.

issues.title: WRECKED look is a muddy pink wash: 60 % comic look + 50 % global red multiply, no backdrop, zoom blur; the pelican is small and half-hidden behind an out-of-focus rider (src/fx/ko/look.ts applyLook 'wrecked', ko/camera.ts side shot)
issues.detail: shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/s-wr-ult.png top row, k-wr-coast-018/036/054.png (fx only). applyLook sets c.ko = 0.6, c.red = 0.5 (col * (1, .32, .3) + .2 red), bgBurst = 0 and zoom 0.03+. The partial blend of the ink/red/paper look with the graded scene, plus the red multiply, flattens the whole frame into pink-salmon at low contrast. The white pelican, the subject, is a small pale shape in the middle, and a huge blurred brown rider in the right foreground covers about a third of the frame for the whole 0.6 s hold. Next to the KO look (strong rays, ink lines), WRECKED reads as an unfinished filter, not a designed 'you got wrecked' panel.
issues.fix: Give WRECKED its own committed palette instead of a half-blend. Use c.ko = 1 with an inverted backdrop (bgBurst = 1, rays in FX_INK on deep red, or a black/white desaturation with only the pelican's reds kept). Drop the global red multiply; put red only in the vignette or a diagonal slash band. Keep zoom <= 0.02 so the subject stays crisp. In the side shot, pick the side with no rider within 2.5 m of the eye-to-pelican segment (track-space test on session riders), else raise the eye. Frame so the pelican body fills >= 35 % of the frame height.

issues.title: Colour grade multiplies the track tint flat over the whole frame (highlights and sky included) and boosts saturation uniformly: whites go cream or orange, the coast sky turns teal, and the mountain's purple sunset becomes monochrome orange-red (src/fx/post/composite-glsl.ts main grade line, src/fx/grade.ts)
issues.detail: Same frame with post on and off (toggles.enabled), mean RGB of patches: coast cloud (243,250,255) -> (250,239,216); coast sky blue channel 248 -> 218 (teal-grey); pelican back (231,226,210) -> (241,220,181) cream. Mountain sky (139,87,156) purple -> (147,61,91) crimson; ridge (126,78,76) -> (141,61,50); pelican back (203,143,129) -> (219,106,67) orange on a brown-red road. City pelican (96,98,153) -> (80,76,165) violet. Evidence: shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/a-coast-cruise(.png|-OFF.png), z-coast-left.png, r-mountain-01-cruise(.png|-OFF.png), z-mtn-cruise-onoff.png, z-mtn-mid.png, z-city-cruise-onoff.png. SPEC section 5 asks for 'gold-pink sunset, layered purple ridges' and a white hero; the grade removes both, and the hero loses figure/ground contrast on every track. The tints come from src/world/looks.ts, but the operator that applies them is fx's.
issues.fix: In the composite, apply the tint luminance-preserving: tintN = uTint / luma(uTint). Apply it as a split-tone weighted to shadows/mid-tones: col *= mix(tintN, vec3(1), smoothstep(0.55, 0.9, l)), so whites and the sky stay clean. Cap its strength (mix 0.5). Replace uniform saturation with vibrance (boost low-saturation pixels more, leave near-white and already-saturated pixels alone). Acceptance: on all three tracks, a pure-white albedo under key light stays within 6 % of neutral, and the mountain sky keeps blue > red*0.8 where the OFF render has it. Add a 'cross-unit: track' note so looks.ts tints get re-tuned against the fixed operator.

issues.title: SHOWTIME impact hold has no subject: the frame is the red burst plus a carpet of ~28 identical white puffs from the shockwave preset, with no victim in view (src/fx/presets/speed.ts shockwave, ko/camera.ts shotFor('ult'))
issues.detail: Real combat SHOWTIME with 3 low-HP rivals (TRIPLE KO), fx only: shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/s-wr-ult.png bottom row, k-ult-coast-132.png, k-ult-coast-180.png. After the impact the comic look and ray burst come on, but the frame holds the pelican cut off at the left edge and a field of same-size, same-colour outlined puffs thrown 7-13 m/s across the road, like popcorn on a red floor. None of the three KO'd riders appears (camera framing also reported by fx-r1-timing). Even with the camera fixed, the uniform puff ring will fill the low third of every ult frame. The game's signature move has the weakest finishing frame of all the cinematics.
issues.fix: shockwave: fewer, larger, varied dust clouds (8-10 puffs, size 0.6-1.6x, two tones with halftone shade). Keep them low (vy <= 1) and fading by 0.45 s, and add a flat ground shock ring (mode 2) instead of a radial carpet. Frame the ult hold on the victims' centroid (as the timing review asks), so the tumbling rivals are the subject against the burst. Check: in the ult hold frames at least one victim body is inside |NDC| < 0.7 and the puffs cover < 15 % of the frame.

issues.title: One plain annulus sprite stands in for most rings: the boost start is an upright 2.2 m magenta hoop round the rider's torso, which looks like a debug gizmo (src/fx/presets/impacts.ts ring(), particles/atlas-shapes.ts ring, presets/speed.ts boost/driftPop)
issues.detail: shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/r-coast-05-boost-a.png, r-city-05-boost-a.png, r-mountain-05-boost-a.png, z-boost-coast-a.png (left). ring() emits a camera-facing billboard of a uniform thin circle. It covers the hero's body for 0.2 s on every drift-boost release. The same generic circle is the block (c-0.png, cyan), sparkle (c-4.png), heal (c-7.png, pink), driftPop, poof and skill rings, so many different events share one look and none of it is comic.
issues.fix: Draw a comic shockwave sprite for the atlas (jagged or segmented, tapering thick to thin, inked edge, a few gaps), and erode it with life. Lay rings that relate to the road flat (mode 2) at the wheel contact; for boost, use a ground ring plus a backward cone of speed spikes behind the wheel, never a hoop around the torso. Give block a hexagon/shield flash, heal rising '+' glyphs, sparkle 4-point glints, so each event reads differently.

issues.title: Landing dust is a perfectly regular circle of identical cream puffs plus a thin ellipse, a mechanical 'cotton-ball wreath' on every hop (src/fx/presets/ground.ts landing)
issues.detail: shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/z-land-coast.png, r-coast-10-land.png, r-coast-11-land.png (all tracks the same), c-2.png. landing() spawns 14 puffs at equal angles (a = i/count*2pi +/- 0.2) with the same colour pair and near-equal size and speed, so they expand as an even ring 2-3 m wide around the bike. That reads as decoration, not a dust kick, and repeats identically each landing.
issues.fix: Bias the burst into a crescent behind and to the sides of the travel direction (angles from the rear 220 deg), randomise size 0.6-1.4x and speed per puff, and use 6-8 larger lead puffs plus small grit (FRAME.stick/drop). Add a second tone or halftone shade on the puffs, and taper the ground ring. Scale count and size with air time (already partly done).

issues.title: World wind lines (mode 5) spawn up to 8 m ahead of the player, so long thin straight lines slice across rivals and hang in the sky like scratches (src/fx/presets/speed.ts streaks, react/emitters.ts streaks)
issues.detail: Slipstream at top speed: a light-blue line crosses the sloth rival's body about 6 m ahead (shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/z-coast-mid.png, visible with post off too, so it is geometry). Boost: 3-5 m straight lines run diagonally through the sky and across the road (shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/z-boost-coast-a.png right, r-coast-06-boost-b-OFF.png). Placement is ahead 0-8 m at radius 1.2-3 m, length = 8 m/s * k (3-5 m), so many lines sit in the centre of the view instead of the periphery where speed lines belong.
issues.fix: Spawn lines from 1 m behind to 2 m ahead of the camera rather than ahead of the rider. Use radius >= 2.5 m with y in 0.3-2.4 m, skip any spawn whose segment passes within 1 m of a rider, shorten to 1.5-2.5 m, and fade alpha by screen distance from the centre so lines live at the edges (the post speed lines already cover the anime look).

issues.title: Edge radial blur is on at plain top speed (no boost or slipstream) and smears the periphery's toon outlines: poles and barrier stripes double and go soft (src/fx/grade.ts SpeedFeel)
issues.detail: Coast at 20.4 m/s (v/top = 1.02), shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/z-coast-left.png: with post on, the left flag pole and the red/white barrier are visibly smeared, the cloud outline is doubled, and the crisp 2-3 px ink lines the art bible relies on are gone in the outer 30 % of the screen. Off, they are sharp. tBlur = 0.018 * smoothstep(0.55, 1.2, v) means normal cruising already pays most of the blur. The progression slow -> top -> boost is right, but the baseline is too blurry for a cel-shaded look.
issues.fix: Start speed blur above 1.05x top speed (boost, slingshot, downhill): tBlur = 0.018 * smoothstep(1.02, 1.3, v) + 0.032 * boost. At normal top speed, convey speed with sparse white edge lines (tLines ~ 0.15) and the camera FOV instead. Keep chroma fringe only in boost.

issues.title: Drift sparks read as a soft coloured glow under the wheel with a few thin streaks; the inked sparks are ~10 px and L3 is not spectacular (src/fx/presets/speed.ts driftSpark/inkSpark)
issues.detail: shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/z-drift-coast.png (L1 blue, L2 orange, L3 pink at 1920x1080, chase cam): colour coding is right, but each tick emits 3 additive streaks of size 0.1 m and at most one inked spark4 (0.22 m, life 0.1-0.16 s). The level mostly reads through the glow blob on the asphalt. From 5 m behind at speed, L2 and L3 differ only in hue. In commercial kart racers the mini-turbo spray is the loudest continuous effect on screen and each tier is bigger than the last.
issues.fix: Scale with level: at L2, 2 inked spark4 per tick at 0.3 m; at L3, 3 at 0.38 m plus a FRAME.zap arc every ~80 ms and hot streaks of size 0.16. Emit from both wheels at L3. Make the level flare a flat ground star (mode 2) rather than a soft glow. Keep the colour order blue -> orange -> pink.

issues.title: Light-hit glow is a soft additive smudge that covers the victim's face, and the hit-stop frames sit under a white wash (src/fx/presets/impacts.ts hit glow, ko/cine.ts flash)
issues.detail: shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/s-hits.png (x-h-light-07): the 0.55 m '#ffe08a' additive glow is a blurry golden blob over the rival's head, the one soft, photographic element in an otherwise inked comic burst (the heavy POW star in x-h-heavy-19 is good). KO strip shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/k-ko-coast-noui-015/018.png: the frozen hit frames are washed grey by post.flash(0.65), so the inked impact star sits in fog (timing review covers the timing).
issues.fix: Replace the hit glow with a 1-2 frame hard-edged white burst sprite (FRAME.burst, inked), or shrink it to 0.3 m with life <= 0.05 s. In KO start, drop the second flash, or make it <= 0.3 with a 1-frame decay, so the frozen frames stay high-contrast.

issues.title: cross-unit: HUD splash, combat ult volume and city road reflections hide or crowd the fx work
issues.detail: ui-hud: the KNOCK OUT splash covers ~70 % of the KO hold from the peak (shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/s-ko-key.png bottom-right, k-ko-coast-072.png). combat: the SHOWTIME impact is a translucent red cylinder plus a vertical beam (shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/k-ult-coast-102.png), which reads as a debug volume. env-city: the wet-road reflections are high-frequency wavy stripes, which fx bloom (0.9) and saturation then amplify (shots/review/fx/r1-art/run4/z-city-cruise-mid.png).
issues.fix: ui-hud: shrink the splash to a diagonal band in the top or bottom third, or delay it until ~250 ms after the peak. combat: replace the cylinder with an inked ground shock ring plus a short vertical flash. env-city: lower the reflection distortion frequency; fx: lower night bloom on mid-tones (threshold 0.7 -> 0.85).
